title: The Morning Build for November 21, 2026: Nvidia CEO Resigns, Anthropic IPO Reaffirms Pacing, Meta Rewrites Net-Zero
intro: Three Big Tech developments landed this week: Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports of multiple affairs and a possible national security probe; Anthropic went public and its CEO recommitted to pacing model training and deployment; and Meta said it is rethinking its 2030 net-zero target because AI data center demand drove record emissions. Each item ties to governance, capital allocation, and operational limits for AI infrastructure.
meta_description: Nvidia’s CEO resignation and congressional testifying deadline, Anthropic’s IPO and pacing pledge, and Meta’s 2030 net-zero rethink after record data center emissions.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after reports of multiple affairs and a national security probe
stories.what_happened: Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation and appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO; reports link one of Huang’s alleged partners to Megaspeed, a firm U.S. officials suspect of channeling Nvidia chips to China, and the Justice Department has taken over an investigation into Megaspeed. Nvidia said it will not reinstate Huang and interim CEO Kress said the company does not plan to sell H200 chips in China.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia supplies most advanced AI accelerators to hyperscalers and enterprises; leadership disruption coincides with active U.S. probes into chip exports and customer relationships, which could affect export policy compliance, board oversight, and strategic relationships with large buyers such as Megaspeed that reportedly purchased billions of dollars in Nvidia chips.
stories.outlook: Jensen Huang is expected to testify before Congress in a closed-door briefing recorded and transcribed before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26, 2026.

stories.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq as CEO Dario Amodei reaffirms commitment to pacing AI training and deployment
stories.what_happened: Anthropic completed its IPO at the Nasdaq opening bell and CEO Dario Amodei used the event to restate the company’s plan to pace model training and deployment and to ‘remain under human control,’ saying the company will take as long as necessary to have confidence systems are safe.
stories.why_it_matters: A public Anthropic converts internal safety commitments into statements to shareholders and regulators; that shifts scrutiny of training cadence and capital allocation into public filings and raises the chance that deployment pacing will appear in forward guidance, SEC disclosures, and public shareholder communications.
stories.outlook: Anthropic’s post-IPO SEC filings and its next quarterly report will be the first public documents to show whether the company’s pacing commitment affects its training schedules, capital plans, or deployment disclosures.

stories.headline: Meta says it is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero goal after record emissions from AI data centers
stories.what_happened: In its 2026 sustainability report, Meta reported total emissions rising from 15.6 million metric tonnes CO2e in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025 and said it is re-evaluating timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones including the 2030 net-zero target because demand for AI infrastructure grew faster than expected.
stories.why_it_matters: Meta’s public retreat on a hard 2030 net-zero timeline signals that hyperscale AI deployments are materially changing energy and capital planning; engineers and infrastructure teams at cloud and hardware vendors should expect continued reliance on mixed power sources and revised interim intensity targets from major hyperscalers.
stories.outlook: Meta’s next sustainability update, the 2027 report, should spell out any revised interim intensity targets and a new timetable for its net-zero ambition.

narration_script: This week’s headlines moved governance, capital, and energy lines across Big Tech. First, Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, one involving an executive at Megaspeed, a company U.S. officials have investigated for suspected chip transfers to China. The Justice Department has taken over the Megaspeed probe, and Nvidia said it will not reinstate Huang and will stop selling H200 chips in China. Jensen Huang is expected to testify before Congress in a closed-door session, with the briefing recorded and transcribed before Thanksgiving on November 26, 2026. Second, Anthropic completed its Nasdaq debut and CEO Dario Amodei used the opening bell to restate a public commitment to pace training and deployment of AI systems and to keep those systems under human control. Turning Anthropic into a public company brings those safety and pacing promises into shareholder and regulatory view, so the company’s post-IPO SEC filings and the next quarterly report will be the first clear signals of whether pacing changes training schedules or capital allocation. Third, Meta’s 2026 sustainability report shows emissions jumped from 15.6 million metric tonnes CO2e in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025. Meta said demand for AI infrastructure grew faster than expected and that it is re-evaluating timelines and interim milestones, including the 2030 net-zero target. The company’s 2027 sustainability report should detail any revised interim intensity targets and a new timetable for its net-zero ambition. Those three items, executive governance and export investigations at Nvidia, public-market scrutiny of Anthropic’s pacing pledge, and Meta’s net-zero rethink driven by data center emissions, create immediate operational and disclosure signals engineers and infra planners should expect in the weeks and quarters ahead.
